subject: Pilot qualification + long-context eval plan for SageWell — next steps
messages:

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pilot qualification + long-context eval plan for SageWell — next steps

Hi Alex / Jordan,

Great to meet you on today's discovery — appreciate you walking us through the chart ingestion workflow and the primary failure modes you're seeing when summarizing long consult notes. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align the pilot scope: 

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: high-fidelity summarization of multi-page consult threads + preserving critical meds/allergies across context windows.
- Primary constraints: heterogeneous doc structure (scanned notes + typed), frequent long appendices, strong non-negotiable accuracy threshold for med/allergy extraction.
- Ops constraint: pilot must run against de-identified sample data in your VPC; you want predictable latency for interactive review (~1–2s per 2k tokens acceptable, higher for full-batch jobs).

Proposed pilot & evaluation plan (short)
1) Data handoff — you provide a 200-document sample (de-identified). We will validate tokenization and truncation distribution.
2) Model candidates — we'll run a small batch against three Redwood-curated variants and surface tradeoffs:
   - rw-long-70b-128k-v1 (recommended for fidelity; higher cost)
   - rw-effic-13b-long-32k (cost-efficient baseline; strong summarization with few-shot prompts)
   - rw-qa-7b-32k (fast reranker for extraction/QA checks)
3) Eval harness — we’ll run the shared prompt set (attached) and measure: truncation rate, answer-level recall for med/allergy fields, ROUGE-L / F1 on extraction tasks, hallucination rate on manually sampled cases.
4) Acceptance criteria — baseline: >= 95% recall on med/allergy extraction, truncation-induced data loss < 1% on sample set, and no major hallucinations in top-10% of failure cases.

Technical asks from SageWell (what we need from you)
- De-identified sample (200 documents) + a short data spec (field/format notes).
- A primary point of contact for security & procurement (to pre-seed the RFI).

Attachments: I attached a 10-document sample template (SageWell-trial-dataset-sample.csv), the prompt set we'll use (SageWell-eval-prompt-set-v1.json), and our preliminary RFI answers for your security team.

Next steps / calendar
- If this sounds right, can you: (a) drop the sample to the Drive link I shared, and (b) confirm the security POC?
- I'll block 60 minutes next week for a kickoff once we have the sample.

Thanks —
Sean
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — good summary.

Couple of clarifying Qs before we drop data: 
- Tokenization/truncation: we have some notes where the signed consent pages are appended and push the clinical narrative beyond 20k tokens in ~5% of docs. Do you expect rw-long-70b-128k to preserve those parts reliably, or will we need to run a pre-aggregation step?
- Cost / throughput: We need a rough estimate for the 200-doc run against the three variants (ballpark tokens per doc ~ 18k average).

Security POC is Jordan (copied). We will aim to upload a de-id sample by EOD Friday.

Also: can you flag any concerns about hallucination detection for medication fields? That is our biggest risk for production.

— Alex
Sr. Data Scientist, SageWell Health

Hi Alex / Jordan — Vanessa here (inference eng). Quick answers inline + suggested config for the pilot.

On tokenization/truncation
- rw-long-70b-128k-v1 is designed for multi-page medical records and preserves prefixes/critical sections by default using prefix-aware KV caching. For the 5% of docs that exceed 20k tokens, we expect the model to retain context if you keep the narrative near the front.
- If critical content lives at the very end (signed pages), we recommend a small pre-processing step to move med/allergy tables into a dedicated metadata block before evaluation. That prevents accidental truncation and is a low-effort change.

On hallucination detection for meds
- We'll include a reranker pass using rw-qa-7b-32k to extract candidate med/allergy items and then run a verifier prompt (few-shot) to check for improbable values (e.g., synthetic drug names or conflicts).
- As part of the eval harness we'll flag any 'extraction confidence < 0.75' cases for manual review so you can measure real-world false positives.

Suggested pilot config (technical)
- Model: rw-long-70b-128k-v1 for primary summarization; rw-effic-13b-long-32k for smaller docs; rw-qa-7b-32k for extraction verification.
- max_context: 131072 tokens (128k) — tune down to 32k for the cost-efficient run.
- steady-state batching: small (N=4) for interactive review; large batch (N=64) for offline full-run.
- caching: enable prefix/KV caching across notes when documents share patient metadata.

Eval metrics we'll produce
- truncation_rate (%) by document length bucket
- med/allergy recall & precision (per-field F1)
- RA (regression alerts) — we'll run pre/post quality checks if you iterate on prompt changes.

I'll provision a sandbox pipeline in your VPC (we support an agent-less storage mount for the trial), but we need the sample and a brief IAM role to mount the data. Sean — can you share the Drive link for upload and I can add engineering instructions?

-Vanessa
Senior Software Engineer, Inference
